The core challenge is balancing supply (available players) with demand (contestant preferences) under hard budget constraints. The four primitives form a compositional hierarchy: popularity weighting shapes the input landscape, performance scaling adjusts individual contributions, salary adjustment modulates cost-benefit tradeoffs, and contestant composition optimization integrates these into feasible team selections. Key failure modes include overfitting noisy popularity data, ignoring correlation structures between positions, and treating discrete decisions as continuous relaxations. To mitigate, we employ conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification and reinforcement learning for adaptive strategy updating.
